Added [wait].max_call_seconds=240 config section; _bounded applies the one-call cap always (a --max-s can shorten, never lengthen past cap); wait/watch use min(max_call_seconds, wait_cap_s); tests/test_wait_cadence.py adds 6 tests (default 240, still-waiting within cap, --max-s still capped, short --max-s honored, resume token, heartbeat renewal). 32 tests pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The 240 s ceiling is only applied inside `ddflow wait`/`watch` (`_call_cap` / `watch` `cap`). The change that was supposed to stop the driver from teaching `for i in seq; sleep 8..20` loops capped near 570 s is not in this change at all (manifest is only wait, watch, `[wait]` config, and tests). An agent that still follows those recipes never enters `_bounded`: given a held file it sleeps in the shell for ~570 s per iteration, so the prompt cache still goes cold and the 11.7 min claim/heartbeat+sleep path in the intent is unchanged. [D-TE-Q3] only constrains the API cap; it does not remove that loop.
